te: Warm community clinics in Bangkok raise delayed transfers of outpatient payments
se: The committee considered progress on a request by the Warm Community Clinic Association to examine delayed transfers of capitation payments for outpatient services (OPCAP) in Bangkok (raised by the chair of the subcommittee concerned). The clinics said this causes a lack of cash, may affect the quality of services and could make service units near people's homes close, and asked that deductions and delays be clearly notified. Proposals are to review the payment mechanism to reflect real costs in Bangkok, open a forum between the NHSO and service units, and add transparency that can be checked. The committee felt that primary care in Bangkok has particular features that differ from the provinces.
it: Request by the Warm Community Clinic Association to examine delayed transfers of outpatient payments (OPCAP) in Bangkok

te: Withdrawal of recognition of a dentistry degree, and help for affected students
se: The committee considered the Thai Dental Council's order withdrawing recognition of the Doctor of Dental Surgery degree of the Faculty of Dentistry, Nation University (curriculum of academic year 2019), which affects students of academic years 2020–2022. A representative of the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation explained that the reasons given in the assessment were the qualifications of the lecturers responsible for the programme and the readiness of clinics and equipment. A group of parents submitted requests such as compensation, help in arranging transfers to accredited institutions, and fair credit transfer. The committee considered the steps for opening programmes, oversight and follow-up, and ways to help the students.
it: Order withdrawing recognition of a Doctor of Dental Surgery degree: opening programmes, oversight and help for students

te: Thai Dental Council announcement on competency criteria for oral hygienists, and the work of dental nurses
se: The committee considered the Thai Dental Council's announcement on competency criteria for oral hygienists (27 Mar 2026), which caused misunderstanding about the work of dental nurses. The Council explained that the announcement aims to develop the primary health care system and does not affect the role of dental nurses already working. It reported 3 problems: the lack of laws that fully cover dental professions, unclear staffing frameworks and career paths, and the lack of a dental staffing framework in sub-district health promoting hospitals transferred to local government. Proposals include having Provincial Administrative Organizations hire dentists, cooperation with the Ministry of Public Health, and more ways for dental nurses to become local government officials. The committee felt the matter should be explained correctly and widely, and stressed prevention because oral health is linked to chronic non-communicable diseases.
it: Thai Dental Council announcement on competency criteria for oral hygienists (27 Mar 2026) and its effect on basic dental services

te: New social security dental benefits (1 May 2026): wisdom tooth surgery, crowns and dental implants
se: The committee considered the dental benefits of insured persons under the new announcement of the Medical Committee, effective 1 May 2026. The Social Security Office explained that the limit of 900 baht a year covers only fillings, scaling and extractions. Wisdom tooth surgery is a separate item of 1,500–2,500 baht depending on difficulty (including X-rays), and new benefits are added: crowns and dental implants. More than 2,000 state and more than 4,000 private facilities take part without patients paying first. Private clinics may charge the difference for fillings, scaling and extractions above 900 baht, but must always tell the insured person first, and may not charge extra for wisdom tooth surgery. At state facilities the benefit can be used without a limit on visits.
it: Structure of dental benefits for insured persons and participation of service units (Social Security Office)

te: Study of the Act on the Summoning Powers of Committees B.E. 2025
se: The committee studied the principles, reasons and scope of the Act on the Summoning Powers of Committees of the House of Representatives and the Senate B.E. 2025, issued under section 129 of the Constitution. It allows committees to issue legally binding orders summoning persons and documents (including electronic documents) instead of asking for cooperation. It removes criminal penalties and uses disciplinary measures for state officials instead. Committees have no power to summon objects other than documents, and the provisions do not yet cover enforcement against members of the public or state officials who are not civil servants. The law is awaiting its regular evaluation every 5 years. The committee made observations so that the law can be used effectively.
it: Principles, scope and results of the Act on the Summoning Powers of Committees B.E. 2025

te: Thailand's medicine security amid global conflicts, and the subcommittees' plans
se: The committee heard progress from 2 subcommittees. It approved moving the field visits and seminars of the primary health care subcommittee to Khon Kaen (7–8 May 2026) and Chanthaburi (28–29 May 2026), and approved setting up a working group in the subcommittee on budget and good governance to draft a National Health Security Bill (No. ..), to propose ways to improve the law so that the system is sustainable. It then studied the country's medicine security in light of conflicts in several regions. The Thai Food and Drug Administration explained its approach in 4 areas, such as measures to oversee the prices of high-cost medicines and medical supplies in emergencies.
it: Primary health care subcommittee: field visits and seminars in Khon Kaen and Chanthaburi rescheduled
Working group set up to draft a National Health Security Bill (No. ..) B.E. ....
Thailand's medicine security in light of conflicts around the world (Thai FDA)

te: Primary care field visits to Chiang Mai and Nonthaburi, and work on the health insurance budget
se: The committee heard progress from 2 subcommittees. The primary health care subcommittee reported on its visit to Chiang Mai, which transferred all its sub-district health promoting hospitals to the Provincial Administrative Organization, in 5 areas: staff, infrastructure, information systems, disease screening, and finance. It also reported on Nonthaburi (20 Feb 2026), which still lacks family medicine doctors and where registration of service units is not yet complete, but which has outreach work such as “Healthy Condos” in urban communities. Proposals include designing staff management to fit the local context and rotating family medicine doctors to provide outreach services. The committee also heard progress from the subcommittee on budget and good governance in the National Health Security system.
it: Progress of the primary health care subcommittee: field visits to Chiang Mai and Nonthaburi
Progress of the subcommittee studying the budget system, management and good governance

te: PCV vaccine (continued): value for money and evaluating the pilot
se: The committee continued with the PCV vaccine, taking the view that making it a basic benefit should use information from all sides. HITAP reported its value-for-money study against the threshold of 160,000 baht per quality-adjusted life year, which depends on the vaccine price, treatment costs, target groups and herd immunity, and stressed that decisions must also consider other factors such as budget impact and equal access. The Health Systems Research Institute explained the design of the study to follow and evaluate the vaccination pilot with the NHSO. The committee also followed the draft announcement on the scope of vaccine services, the results of the public hearing and progress on buying the vaccine.
it: Main points of the draft announcement on the scope of PCV vaccine services, public hearing results and procurement progress

te: PCV vaccine (continued): how new vaccines are added, with information from HITAP and the National Vaccine Institute
se: The committee continued with the PCV vaccine, inviting the NHSO, the Health Intervention and Technology Assessment Program Foundation (HITAP) and the National Vaccine Institute. The National Vaccine Institute explained that a new vaccine is added through 3 mechanisms: the subcommittee on immunisation, the subcommittee on the National List of Essential Medicines, which considers value for money and budget burden, and the subcommittee under the National Health Security Board, which considers adding it to the benefit package. Work to introduce the PCV vaccine has gone on since 2017, including a pilot project in Maha Sarakham and the listing of PCV10 and PCV13 in the National List of Essential Medicines.
it: Policy on access to the PCV vaccine (NHSO, HITAP and the National Vaccine Institute)

te: Vaccine against severe pneumococcal pneumonia (PCV) for Thai children
se: The committee considered the policy on access to the PCV vaccine for Thai children under the National Health Security system, inviting the NHSO, the Department of Disease Control and the Royal College of Pediatricians of Thailand. It learned that the National Health Security Board approved a pilot of PCV vaccination in provinces or health regions with high illness rates that are ready to evaluate results, using the National Health Security Fund. The NHSO was asked to work with the Health Systems Research Institute and the Department of Disease Control to design an evaluation within 1 year, and to negotiate a price as close as possible to that of UNICEF or GAVI. The NHSO said it had proposed a new benefit of about 225 million baht, which the Cabinet has approved.
it: Policy on access to vaccines against severe pneumococcal disease for Thai children (NHSO, Department of Disease Control, Royal College of Pediatricians)

te: Policy report on the health workforce: safe staff, safe patients
se: The committee considered the draft report of the subcommittee on medical personnel, “Policy Proposals on Managing, Developing and Retaining the Health Workforce”. Key proposals include that staff safety equals patient safety, by pushing a draft act to protect the work of public health personnel that sets safe working hours; planning staff according to the real workload of each area; and fair pay according to workload and risk, with urgent, medium-term and long-term plans. The committee added observations such as spreading staff fairly across areas, the proportions in which staff are trained, and promoting family medicine doctors in every area.
it: Draft report “Policy Proposals on Managing, Developing and Retaining the Health Workforce”

te: 2 draft NHSO announcements on innovative service units: reasons and effects
se: The committee heard the intent and effects of 2 draft announcements of the National Health Security Office on paying for innovative medical services. Innovative service units are a partnership between private providers and the NHSO so that people can reach primary care easily and crowding in state hospitals is reduced. They grew to 7 types in 2024 under the “30 baht, treatment anywhere” policy. Today there are about 10,000 units, used about 31 million times in 2025. New rates include 100 baht per visit for diagnosis and advice, or 180 baht per visit including medicine and services (previously 320 baht). The NHSO explained 3 reasons: the risk of the budget growing out of control under open-ended payment, irregular claims found in some cases, and value for money compared with real costs.
it: Intent and effects of the draft NHSO announcements on paying for innovative medical services (2 announcements)

te: Effects of draft NHSO announcements on warm community clinics (innovative service units)
se: Meeting on Tuesday 13 January 2026, according to the meeting notice. The agenda was a study of the facts on the problems and effects of drafting announcements of the National Health Security Office (NHSO), with groups of doctors and operators of warm community clinics (innovative service units) invited to give information. (The Senate published the meeting summary as an image file. Please read the details in the original documents below.)
it: Problems and effects of the draft NHSO announcements (hearing from groups of doctors and operators of warm community clinics)

te: Planning the subcommittees' work: primary health care and the health insurance budget
se: The committee considered how its subcommittees will work. The subcommittee following primary health care set a framework to follow results after the Primary Health System Act B.E. 2019 in 5 areas: policy and plans, laws and rules, registration and standards of service units, service delivery, and staffing. It chose field visits to 5 areas, Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Khon Kaen, Nonthaburi and Narathiwat, to cover service units already transferred to local government and those not yet transferred, and areas with different levels of readiness. It will then invite the agencies that train health workers to find ways to solve staff shortages, before reporting to the committee. The committee also considered the work plan of the subcommittee studying the budget system, management and good governance under the National Health Security system.
it: Work plan of the Subcommittee to Follow Progress on the Primary Health Care System (field visits to 5 areas)
Work plan of the Subcommittee to Study the Budget System, Management and Good Governance under the National Health Security System

te: Seminar results and the draft report on public hospital finances
se: The meeting considered the results of the subcommittee's seminar "Raising the efficiency and financial sustainability of public hospitals: from findings to policy options" held on 21 October 2026. Participants agreed with the findings and added 5 points, such as assessing finances with several indicators, separating the cost of services from the cost of readiness, and linking service quality with financial sustainability. The survey's top 3 priorities were budget allocation and payment mechanisms, a medium-term health financing framework, and the health workforce. The meeting then considered the draft study report, with 8 findings, 9 proposals and 6 chapters, and asked for a clear implementation framework for each proposal before the report goes to the committee, the government and the agencies concerned.
it: Results of the seminar "Raising the efficiency and financial sustainability of public hospitals: from findings to policy options"
Draft study report (8 findings, 9 proposals)
